title: Chapter 4 Mastery Quiz: The Psychoanalytic Revolution & Psychodynamics
description: Demonstrate comprehensive mastery of Freud's unconscious, structural model, defenses, and Neo-Freudians Jung, Adler, and Horney.

questions.question: What was Sigmund Freud's original medical profession before developing psychoanalysis?
questions.explanation: Freud was a clinical neurologist in Vienna conducting laboratory research on nerve cells and treating nervous disorders.

questions.question: Which historic case study, co-authored with Josef Breuer in 'Studies on Hysteria' (1895), launched psychoanalytic therapy?

options.text: The case of Anna O. (Bertha Pappenheim)

questions.explanation: Bertha Pappenheim (pseudonym Anna O.) was Josef Breuer's patient whose treatment catalyzed the development of psychoanalysis.

questions.question: In Freud's topographical model of mind, which region is completely submerged and holds instinctual drives and repressed memories?
questions.explanation: The Unconscious represents the vast submerged portion of the mind containing instinctual drives and repressed thoughts.

questions.question: What therapeutic technique replaced hypnosis as Freud's primary method for accessing unconscious conflicts?
questions.explanation: Freud developed Free Association, encouraging patients to speak spontaneously without filtering or self-censorship.

questions.question: In Freud's 1900 book 'The Interpretation of Dreams', what did he call dreams?

options.text: The royal road to the unconscious
A chemical byproduct of REM paralysis

questions.explanation: Freud famously declared that dream interpretation is the 'via regia'—the royal road to the knowledge of the unconscious mind.

questions.question: What is the difference between manifest content and latent content in dream analysis?

options.text: Manifest is the remembered surface storyline; Latent is the disguised unconscious meaning
Manifest is black-and-white; Latent is in color
Manifest occurs in animals; Latent occurs only in humans
Manifest is verbal; Latent is motor reflex

questions.explanation: Manifest content is the conscious narrative remembered upon waking; latent content is the hidden unconscious wish.

questions.question: According to Freud's structural model, which psychic agency operates on the 'pleasure principle' and seeks immediate gratification?
questions.explanation: The Id is the primitive, instinctual agency driven entirely by the pleasure principle to satisfy biological urges immediately.

questions.question: Which personality agency represents the internalized moral standards, conscience, and guilt of society?
questions.explanation: The Superego internalizes societal taboos and moral guidelines, rewarding good behavior with pride and punishing transgressions with guilt.

questions.question: What term describes the psychological phenomenon where a patient unconsciously redirects emotions about early authority figures onto their therapist?
questions.explanation: Transference occurs when the patient projects feelings and expectations from past relational figures onto the analyst.

questions.question: Which defense mechanism is considered the foundational cornerstone upon which all other defense mechanisms are built?
questions.explanation: Repression—the involuntary banishment of anxiety-provoking thoughts into the unconscious—is the master defense mechanism.

questions.question: A person who is unconsciously dishonest accuses everyone else in their office of lying and stealing. What defense mechanism is operating?
questions.explanation: Projection involves attributing one's own unacceptable impulses or traits onto other people.

questions.question: What is the chronological sequence of Freud's five psychosexual stages of development?
questions.explanation: Freud's stages proceed from Oral (infancy), Anal (toddler), Phallic (early childhood), Latency (middle childhood), to Genital (adolescence onward).

questions.question: In Freudian theory, what is the Oedipus Complex, occurring during the phallic stage?

options.text: A child's unconscious sexual desire for the opposite-sex parent and rivalry with the same-sex parent
A fear of being separated from peer groups at school
The adult instinct to achieve creative career success
An innate terror of darkness and open heights

questions.explanation: The Oedipus complex involves unconscious incestuous desires toward the opposite-sex parent accompanied by guilt and rivalry toward the same-sex parent.

questions.question: Why did philosopher Karl Popper criticize Freudian psychoanalysis as unscientific?

options.text: Because it was unfalsifiable—no possible behavioral observation could ever disprove it
Because it used too many statistical formulas
Because Freud was not an Austrian citizen

questions.explanation: Popper argued that because psychoanalysis could flexibly explain any conflicting outcome after the fact, it was not falsifiable and therefore not genuine empirical science.

questions.question: What primary reason led Carl Jung to break his professional relationship with Freud in 1913?

options.text: Jung rejected Freud's overemphasis on sexual drive as the sole root of human psychology
Jung wanted to abandon all clinical therapy
Freud refused to publish in German journals

questions.explanation: Jung believed libido was a broader, generalized life energy rather than exclusively sexual, leading to the bitter 1913 break.

questions.question: What did Carl Jung term the deep, inherited ancestral layer of the human mind containing universal archetypes?
questions.explanation: Jung postulated the Collective Unconscious as a transpersonal, evolutionary substrate shared by all humans across civilizations.

questions.question: In Jungian psychology, what archetype represents the social mask or public face an individual shows to the world?
questions.explanation: The Persona (from the Latin for theater mask) is the public facade we cultivate to conform to cultural and social demands.

questions.question: Which personality dimension pair was introduced by Carl Jung and later adopted into popular personality inventories like the MBTI?
questions.explanation: Jung defined Introversion (inward orientation toward subjective thought) and Extraversion (outward orientation toward external objects).

questions.question: According to Alfred Adler, what fundamental psychological challenge drives human personality and behavior?

options.text: Overcoming the universal feeling of inferiority and striving for competence

questions.explanation: Adler posited that because all infants are born dependent and weak, personality is driven by striving to overcome inferiority toward mastery.

questions.question: What German term did Alfred Adler use for 'social interest'—the hallmark of psychological health?
questions.explanation: Gemeinschaftsgefühl (community feeling / social interest) was Adler's benchmark for mental health—caring for the welfare of others.

questions.question: How did Karen Horney counter Sigmund Freud's theory of 'penis envy'?

options.text: She argued women envy male social privilege and power, and proposed that men experience 'womb envy'
She claimed women possess no unconscious mind
She proved that biology alone determines all gender differences
She argued that infants have no relationship with mothers

questions.explanation: Horney asserted that women envied the patriarchal rights granted to men, and suggested men unconsciously envied women's ability to create life ('womb envy').

questions.question: What are Karen Horney's three major neurotic coping strategies for managing basic anxiety?

options.text: Moving toward people, moving against people, moving away from people

questions.explanation: Horney outlined three relational styles: compliance (moving toward), hostility/power (moving against), and detachment/isolation (moving away).
